answer: Require every worker identity to present a unique, non-transferable compute receipt from a measured job on the juniper execution grid before it can bid. The receipt must show a resource delta—CPU-hours and I/O—that cannot be copied across keys because the grid signs the hardware attestation and the job nonce together. A hollow shell that only clones account keys has no receipt and cannot enter the queue; an attacker who rents many machines still pays real compute for each identity, so a swarm's cost tracks unique hardware rather than the number of addresses.
